history.summary: Budharaja Temple is the hilltop Shiva temple of Sambalpur city, Odisha, standing on Budharaja Hill (also the locality name) with panoramic views of the city and the Mahanadi. The IGNCA/ASI record (ORSMLPR006) dates it to the Chauhan rule of the Sambalpur State, 18th century AD (first quarter). Other accounts give King Chhatrasal (1690-1705 AD), seventh Chauhan ruler of Sambalpur, as the initiator, completed by his son King Ajith Singh, and say it was built to commemorate the death of prince Burha Rai; one travel site instead claims a 14th-15th century origin under the first Chauhan king Balaram Dev (verify - the 18th-century IGNCA dating is the most authoritative source located). Architecturally it is a rekha vimana with pidha jagamohana and an open pillared mandapa porch, later plastered and whitewashed; the jagamohana walls carry a twelve-armed dancing Shiva and an eight-armed Mahishasuramardini. Budharaja hill has 1857 associations: Veer Surendra Sai is said to have used the hill to watch British troop movements. A well behind the temple is fenced and reputed to connect by a secret tunnel to Raja Bakhri, Rani Bakhri and Gopalji Math (verify). A Shahid Stambha commemorates freedom fighters. The temple is under the care of the Siva Bhagat committee. No CSV correction needed: town Sambalpur and district Sambalpur are correct.

travel.airport: Veer Surendra Sai Airport, Jharsuguda, approximately 63 km (verify); Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar, is a farther option.
travel.railway: Sambalpur Junction, approximately 5 km from the temple (verify).
travel.road: About 3 km from Sambalpur Bus Stand; a concrete road leads up the hill and 108-200 steps (sources vary) reach the top; right side of the road from Ainthapali bus stand toward Laxmi talkies.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; evenings before sunset for views. Visit on Shivaratri or Sital Sasthi for the grandest festival atmosphere.
